about:
I'm a software developer and artist-researcher based in Montreal.

I build computers for agents: machines that autonomous software can inhabit for a long time. My part is core storage, the state that has to survive for that to work.

I also make protocol art. I treat systems and protocols as environments: the work is a set of rules, and the art is whatever keeps happening once people and machines start following them. It is never quite finished. These works live in the browser, and lately they are about artificial intelligence: every photo on my phone published only as words, a model that slowly deletes its own origin, agents that negotiate what an artwork is worth.

Before all this, I planted over a million trees. It left me thinking of software as site-specific: each tree went into one particular patch of ground, and a system takes root the same way, in situ.
projects_A:
I build computers for agents, working on the storage underneath them: what lets a long-running machine be interrupted and come back knowing what it knew.

I also make protocol art: browser-native works about artificial intelligence where the rules are the medium. Each one is its own small environment that humans and agents can watch, read, and join, and it keeps evolving as they do.

Go to [vincentcharlebois.net](https://vincentcharlebois.net) for earlier research-driven work; tell your AI agent to read `portfolio.md` for a short selection of current projects.
